clue.text: Greeting from one again and again denied preferment?

definitions.text: from one again and again denied preferment?

blocks.note: first meaning: a jokey hello to someone you haven't met for ages

blocks.clueFragment: from one again and again denied preferment?
blocks.note: second meaning: a cleric passed over for years, never given a bishop's diocese

explanation.walkthrough: A see is the diocese of a bishop, and preferment is promotion in the church, so a priest repeatedly overlooked has gone a long time with no see.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a familiar informal salutation used when meeting an old friend after a long absence.

clue.text: Person misusing horse? Put on an extra court

blocks.note: to put on more is to add
an means one, and one is the Roman numeral I
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A rider mistreats a horse, then a further tennis court is laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, so the person misusing it is not a rider at all. 'Extra' only reinforces the idea of putting something on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abuses heroin is a drug dependent, a habitual user of the narcotic.

clue.text: Doctor Galen with niece: not Grace?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Galen, the ancient physician, has a niece who is not called Grace.
explanation.walkthrough: Galen was a famous Greek physician, which makes 'Doctor' read as his title; Grace looks like the niece's name but is the quality being negated.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace means poise and refinement of movement, so its absence is clumsiness or lack of polish.

clue.text: Person with assured belief Arkwright heard?

indicators.note: something heard reaches the ear only, so we want a spelling that matches the spoken sound

blocks.note: a wright is a builder, and the builder of the Ark was Noah

explanation.surface: Someone who is sure of their faith listens to Arkwright, perhaps the inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright looks like Richard Arkwright of the spinning frame; read it as ark-wright, the man who built the Ark. In a non-rhotic accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: One who knows something holds it as certain truth, which is a confident conviction rather than mere opinion.

clue.text: Easy opportunity to bag stray reptile

indicators.note: to bag is to put into a sack, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: a tap-in is an easy goal from very close range
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A hunter gets a simple chance to catch a wandering reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: A tap-in is a football term for a goal that only needs a gentle touch.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small freshwater turtle, an example of the cold-blooded scaly animal class.

clue.text: Kitty after second little bit

indicators.note: 'after' means following, so the earlier-named word is written behind the later one

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the kitty in a card game is the pot of stakes

explanation.surface: A cat comes along a moment behind something small.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a cat but is the pool of money in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot of something is a small amount, as in a spot of lunch, an everyday British idiom.

clue.text: Revolutionary husband taking place in battle

blocks.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
H is the abbreviation for husband
an event that is on is happening

explanation.surface: A rebel husband takes his position in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Marat was murdered in his bath, a famous painting by David; the long race takes its name from the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathon was the battle of 490 BC where the Athenians defeated the invading Persians.

clue.text: Exhibitionist regrets surgery after lift

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something raises it, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
an op is an operation

explanation.surface: A show-off is sorry about the cosmetic operation that followed a facelift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' tempts as a facelift, which fits the surgery; it is the signal to read the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strikes attitudes to impress others is putting on an affected show.

clue.text: Put steps outside at home with men planning

indicators.note: putting something outside means wrapping it around, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
a dance is a set of steps
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Steps are put outside the house as soldiers plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The men come first in the answer though last in the clue: the word 'with' simply adds them.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense the word means orderly arrangement or disposition, the act of arranging a design.

clue.text: Scottish John stops Pilot Officer in quiet passage

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so one piece is inserted to close up another

blocks.note: PO is the RAF rank abbreviation
Ian is the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: A Scot named John halts an RAF officer in a hushed corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests a corridor; in music it is a section of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical stretch marked to be played softly carries this Italian dynamic marking.

clue.text: Good and bad to host initially riotous quiz

indicators.note: a host takes in guests, so the outer piece receives another inside it
initially means at the start, so only a word's opening letter is used

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
ill means bad, as in ill effects
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Good and bad people host a wild quiz night.
explanation.walkthrough: Good and bad together make one word, which then takes in the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to interrogate them relentlessly with questions.

clue.text: Does this foresee terrible cost, recession and a war?

definitions.text: Does this foresee terrible cost, recession and a war?

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forecaster asks whether expense, slump and conflict are all in store.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the mixed letters of the three disasters are what the gloomiest forecast predicts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the most pessimistic projection of events, exactly a prediction of costs, slump and conflict.

clue.text: Two for one for example in Bury

indicators.note: a thing that is in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A two-for-one deal is offered in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, and 'two for one' like a shop offer; read 'Two, for one' as giving an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is one instance of a whole number, a numeral without any fractional part.

clue.text: Who might steal eggs — and slowly cook them?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who takes game or birds' eggs illegally
second meaning: a pan with cups for cooking eggs gently in simmering water

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is loose: the thing that slowly cooks eggs is a kitchen pan, so the clue reads 'what might slowly cook them'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an illicit hunter on someone else's land and a utensil for simmering eggs.

clue.text: Anger on stage in a cast

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown about and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tempers flare on stage among the members of a theatre cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' fits the theatre picture as the actors; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke hostility in someone is to make them cross, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Ascetic at last departing for Ruhr location

indicators.note: the final part leaving means the word loses its closing letter

blocks.note: a member of a self-denying Jewish sect of Roman times

explanation.surface: A hermit finally leaves for somewhere in Germany's industrial heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Essenes, the sect linked with the Dead Sea Scrolls, give ESSENE; dropping the last E leaves ESSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This German city lies in the Ruhr valley, the coal and steel region of North Rhine-Westphalia.

clue.text: See 12
Study Hesiod's conclusion in French

indicators.note: a conclusion is an ending, so only the word's final letter is taken

blocks.note: closing letter of the poet's name
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A student examines how the Greek poet Hesiod ends, in a French version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb about reading Hesiod, but it is a noun for a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a small private room for work or retreat, much like a study in a house.

clue.text: Terrible blow where driest winds circling it

indicators.note: something that winds twists and turns, so the letters are twisted into a new order
to circle something is to go round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A dreadful drought where the parched winds swirl around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' reads as gusts of air in a desert; it is a verb meaning twists. 'It' for sex appeal is an old convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a severe misfortune, and 'blow' here means a shock or setback.

clue.text: One donning Great King's spun garment

indicators.note: donning is putting on clothes, so one piece is worn by and enclosed in another
something spun is turned round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Cnut the Great, also Canute, was king of England, Denmark and Norway
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone puts on the robe a great king had woven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spun' suggests the cloth was spun from thread; it turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose sleeveless body-covering is an item of clothing worn since ancient times.

clue.text: Cut down knight in cold Danish city

indicators.note: a thing placed in another goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Odense is a city in Denmark, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight is struck down in a chilly Danish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' reads as killed in battle; here it means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text by reducing its length is to abridge it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Old Greek university plugging dissertations

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one piece is pushed into the middle of another

blocks.note: theses are long academic dissertations
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An elderly Greek university is promoting its students' dissertations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Greek' looks like it describes the university; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus was the mythical Athenian hero who killed the Minotaur in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: Watch insect here shedding wings

indicators.note: wings are the outer edges, so losing them strips a word's first and last letters

blocks.note: a tick is a small bloodsucking arachnid, loosely an insect
the word with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: Look at this insect here as it loses its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' reads as an order to look; it is the noun for a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is old slang for a pocket timepiece, named for the sound it makes.

clue.text: Cosmonaut, wildly enthusiastic, to call shortly

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to be gaga about something is to be infatuated
ring, to phone, without its last letter

explanation.surface: An excited space traveller is about to phone home soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon'; it means the word is cut short. To ring someone is British for to phone them.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin was the Soviet spaceman who became the first human to orbit the Earth in 1961.

clue.text: Sinister Parisian displaying 3

blocks.note: first meaning: the French word for left, as sinister is the Latin and heraldic left
second meaning: socially awkward and clumsy, the answer to 3 down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' tempts as menacing, but in heraldry it means left-hand; a Parisian would say the same word for left. The 3 points to the answer of 3 down, a lack of grace.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword for left-handed came to mean awkward or tactless in English, the opposite of deft.

clue.text: Bad hat seen in opera (Scala)

indicators.note: something seen within words is visible inside them, so the letters are found running through the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An unpleasant hat is spotted at an opera at La Scala in Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad hat' reads like a fashion disaster at the opera house; it is old slang for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad hat is an old-fashioned phrase for a rogue or mischievous wrongdoer.

clue.text: Romanian dictator stops hoarding uranium and copper

indicators.note: to hoard is to store something away, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: to cease is to stop
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A tyrant halts the stockpiling of uranium and copper.
explanation.walkthrough: Both metals become their chemical symbols; the dictator's name is famously awkward to spell, so the wordplay lays it out letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolae Ceausescu was the Communist ruler of Romania, overthrown and executed in 1989.

clue.text: Fourth man group hated at first

indicators.note: at first means at the very start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a set is a group
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The fourth member of the band was disliked by the group from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the first men are Adam, Cain and Abel, so the next born is the fourth man.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve, born after the murder of Abel, the fourth male in the Bible.

clue.text: See 1
Be patronising towards women denied sons

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a man who patronises women is chauvinist
S is the abbreviation for son, here removed

explanation.surface: A father condescends to the women of the family after his sons are kept away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be patronising' looks like a single verb phrase; 'Be' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is simply to have being or reality, the verb of living and occurring.

clue.text: Book in Spanish English twice revised

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English, used two times

explanation.surface: A book in Spanish and English has been edited twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bilingual edition; the book is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesians is a letter of Paul in the New Testament, one of the books of the Bible.
